title: Nonempty opens in a high-dimensional Noetherian local domain are infinite
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak n)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a local integral domain: $\mathfrak n$ is its unique maximal ideal and $ab=0$ implies $a=0$ or $b=0$. If the Krull dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] is at least $2$, then every nonempty open subset $O\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ is infinite.

proof.text: Suppose, for a contradiction, that a nonempty open $O\subseteq X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is finite. Since $R$ is a nonzero domain, $(0)$ is prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes](1), its closure is $V(0)=X$, so $(0)\in O$: otherwise the closed complement of $O$ would contain that closure. For each $\mathfrak p\in O\setminus\{(0)\}$ its closure is $V(\mathfrak p)$ and does not contain $(0)$, since $\mathfrak p\nsubseteq(0)$. The finite union $F=\bigcup_{\mathfrak p\in O\setminus\{(0)\}}V(\mathfrak p)$ is closed, and $O\setminus F=\{(0)\}$ is open in $X$. Thus the finite-open assumption makes the generic singleton open.

source.place: Tag 02IG, lemma-Noetherian-local-domain-dim-2-infinite-opens, first three sentences of the proof; closures as in Tag 00ES, lemma-irreducible(1).

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] to read $\dim X$ as the supremum of lengths of prime-ideal chains in $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters], $d=\dim R$ is a finite integer. Thus $d\geq2$. In particular $X$ is not a singleton, since a singleton has no chain of irreducible closed subsets of positive length.

source.place: Tag 02IG, dimension hypothesis and the integer dim(R) in its proof; Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension.

proof.text: Apply the basis clause of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] to the open $\{(0)\}$ at $(0)$. It gives $x\in R$ with $(0)\in D(x)\subseteq\{(0)\}$; hence $D(x)=\{(0)\}$ and $x\ne0$. Also $x$ is not a unit, since no prime contains a unit and otherwise $D(x)=X$, contrary to Step 2. In a local ring the nonunits are precisely the unique maximal ideal, so $x\in\mathfrak n$. This is the $x$ chosen in the source.

source.place: Tag 02IG, the choice of x and the equality D(x)={(0)}; basis supplied by Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology(14).

proof.text: The quotient $\bar R=R/xR$ is a nonzero Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak n}=\mathfrak n/xR$. Indeed its ideals are the ideals of $R$ containing $xR$, modulo $xR$; finite generators descend, and maximal ideals correspond under inverse image, so the unique maximal ideal descends. The quotient is nonzero since $x\in\mathfrak n$. As $R$ is a domain and $x\ne0$, $xr=0$ implies $r=0$, so $x$ is a nonzerodivisor. Now [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] gives $\dim\bar R=d-1\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 02IG, the application of Tag 00KW, lemma-one-equation, to the nonzero element x in the maximal ideal; elementary quotient-ideal description made explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters] to $\bar R$. Choose $\bar y_2,\ldots,\bar y_d\in\bar{\mathfrak n}$ whose generated ideal $\bar J$ has radical $\bar{\mathfrak n}$, and choose the exponent $N\geq1$ supplied there with $\bar{\mathfrak n}^{N}\subseteq\bar J$. Lift them to $y_2,\ldots,y_d\in\mathfrak n$ and put $I=(x,y_2,\ldots,y_d)$. The inverse image of $\bar J$ is exactly $I$, since the quotient kernel is $xR$. For $a\in\mathfrak n$ the class of $a^N$ is in $\bar J$, hence $a^N\in I$. Conversely $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$, and primality of $\mathfrak n$ implies that $a^r\in I$ for $r\geq1$ forces $a\in\mathfrak n$. Consequently $\sqrt I=\mathfrak n$: the $d$ elements $x,y_2,\ldots,y_d$ generate an ideal of definition in $R$.

source.place: Tag 02IG, selection of an ideal of definition in R/xR using Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, and lifting it to R; the power clause of the cited node supplies the explicit radical calculation.

proof.text: Permute these $d$ generators to the order $y_2,x,y_3,\ldots,y_d$; their generated ideal is still $I$. All lie in $\mathfrak n$, $\sqrt I=\mathfrak n$, and their number is $d=\dim R$. Since $d\geq2$, [lem-per-partial-parameters-quotient-dimension] applies with $i=1$ and $i=2$, giving $\dim(R/(y_2))=d-1$ and $\dim(R/(y_2,x))=d-2$. No regularity or Cohen–Macaulay hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 02IG, the two quotient dimension equalities, by Tag 02IE, lemma-elements-generate-ideal-definition, after reordering parameters.

proof.text:
The first equality in Step 6 implies $y_2
e0$: if $y_2=0$ then $R/(y_2)=R$ has dimension $d$, not $d-1$. Suppose every prime $\mathfrak p$ containing $y_2$ also contained $x$. For any ideal $J$, inverse image along $R	o R/J$ identifies primes of $R/J$ with primes of $R$ containing $J$: the inverse sends $\mathfrak p$ to $\mathfrak p/J$, prime because $(R/J)/(\mathfrak p/J)=R/\mathfrak p$ is a domain. These inverse operations preserve and reflect strict inclusion. Under the supposition, the prime chains for $R/(y_2)$ and $R/(y_2,x)$ are thus the same chains in $R$, so their suprema, hence their dimensions [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], agree. This contradicts $d-1
e d-2$. Therefore there is a prime $\mathfrak p$ containing $y_2$ but not $x$. It lies in $D(x)=\{(0)\}$, yet is nonzero since it contains $y_2
e0$. This final contradiction rules out finite $O$, as required.
